newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX NIKKEI FUTURES END WEAK, SENTIMENT BEARISH.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX NIKKEI FUTURES END WEAK, SENTIMENT BEARISH.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures slid below the key 19,500 level on Thursday as pessimism about Japan's construction and financial sectors weighed on the market.
Dealers said further falls were likely as players were anxious about more financial institutions being implicated in a racketeer payoff scandal.
"When there's good news, people hesitate to buy. But if there's any bad news, they just sell," a senior dealer at a Japanese brokerage said.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract lost 345 points to end at 19,370 after backing off from an early high of 19,750.
"We'll probably trade between 19,200 and 19,600 tomorrow. But by next week, we should be heading for 18,500. I'm going to stay short on the Nikkei," the dealer added.
A trader at a U.S. futures house said the September Nikkei might try to test the 19,800 barrier again before coming off. But he also said the market was likely to head for 18,500 soon.
Taiwan stock index futures ended lower as Taipei shares failed to take their cue from Wall Street's impressive close amid soaring Taiwan money rates.
The August MSCI contract ended down 3.7 to 409.9 on volume of 1,710 lots.
The Japanese brokerage dealer said the breach of the 410 level opened the way for further declines. "It looks like it can go lower but I'd start to buy around 390," he said.
